newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cigarette mkt stable in 96 - Philip Morris.
newsitem.headline: German cigarette mkt stable in 96 - Philip Morris.

text.p: Germany's market for cigarettes remained relatively stable in 1996 with sales for the year expected at 168.4 billion cigarettes compared with 169.6 billion in 1995, the German unit of U.S. tobacco giant Philip Morris said late on Monday.
Turnover from cigarettes including taxes will stand at 35.6 billion marks, up from 34.9 billion marks, Paul Hendrys, managing director of Philip Morris GmbH, told a news conference.
Philip Morris increased its market share to 41.4 percent this year from 40.1 percent in 1995 and its sales are expected to rise to 11.5 billion marks from 10.94 billion including tax, Hendrys said.
Tobacco tax accounts for about 8.2 billion marks of sales this year, up from 7.85 billion last year, Hendrys said.
Pre-tax profit this year will match the 1995 level of 447 million marks, Hendrys said.

The company has invested a total of 96.6 million marks at its three sites in Berlin, Dresden and Munich this year. Hendrys said Philip Morris could only hold on to the sites if their productivity rose to compensate for high costs.
The company employs about 3,630 people in Germany, compared with 3,675 last year. -- Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756526
